text:
Liam: Heads up — CloudVendor issued a promotional credit that was applied then reversed mid-billing cycle. Vendor invoice landed after the reversal. Need consensus for 2024-11 close: accrue payable or treat as deferral? Total credit $27,420.

Priya: Are these vendor-funded reimbursements or customer-facing discounts we owe back?

Liam: Vendor-funded reimbursement. Applied on 2024-11-10, reversal ran 2024-11-14, vendor invoice dated 2024-11-19. We had recognized revenue on 5 invoices. Split below:
acct-777: $11,200 (prepaid annual)
acct-888: $8,120 (usage billed)
acct-999: $8,100 (prepaid quarterly)

Jon: For usage-billed amounts reverse immediately against recognized revenue. For prepaid contracts, create a revenue deferral adjustment and amortize over remaining term. Because vendor invoice exists and payment ETA is <60 days, we can set a vendor accrual.

Priya: Draft JE suggestion:
Dr Revenue Deferral (2100) 27,420
  Cr Vendor Accrual (2200) 27,420
Then for usage reversal:
Dr Revenue (4000) 8,120
  Cr Revenue Deferral (2100) 8,120

Liam: Vendor PO CV-5544, payment ETA 2024-12-07, I'll attach vendor email. Tag memos "CloudVendor promo reversal" and route to finance-leads@redwood.com.

accounting-bot: Reminder — month close lock 2024-11-30 23:59 PST. Please submit supporting schedules with invoice mapping before 2024-11-29 EOD.

Jon: I'll prepare the amortization schedules per account and route the JE for approval. Priya — can you confirm GL mappings and sign-off workflow?

Priya: Confirmed GLs above. Workflow: route to FP&A for >$20k, attach vendor invoice, include per-invoice IDs. I'll review once uploaded. :thumbsup:
